Other things being equal, a modest ornithologist would prefer a place where he could stand still and look up without becoming himself a gazing-stock. arxiv-1603-09416.title: Search for the primordial gravitational waves with Very Long Baseline Interferometry
arxiv-1603-09416.creator: Oleg Titov
arxiv-1603-09416.description: Abstract Some models of the expanding Universe predict that the astrometric proper motion of distant radio sources embedded in space-time are non-zero as the radial distance from observer to the source grows. Systematic proper motion effects would produce a predictable quadrupole pattern on the sky that could be detected using Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) technique.

arxiv-2107-13400.title: Fourier transform of surface–carried measures of two-dimensional generic surfaces and applications
arxiv-2107-13400.creator: Jean-Claude Cuenin, Robert Schippa
arxiv-2107-13400.description: Abstract . We give a simple proof of the sharp decay of the Fourier-transform of surface-carried measures of two-dimensional generic surfaces. The estimates are applied to prove Strichartz and resolvent estimates for elliptic operators whose characteristic surfaces satisfy the generic assumptions. We also obtain new results on the spectral and scattering theory of discrete Schrödinger operators on the cubic lattice.

arxiv-2302-07820.title: Equilibria of large random Lotka-Volterra systems with vanishing species: a mathematical approach
arxiv-2302-07820.creator: Imane Akjouj (1) , Walid Hachem (2) , Mylène Maïda (1),(3) , Jamal Najim (2)
arxiv-2302-07820.description: Abstract . Ecosystems with a large number of species are often modelled as Lotka-Volterra dynamical systems built around a large random interaction matrix. Under some known conditions, a global equilibrium exists and is unique. In this article, we rigorously study its statistical properties in the large dimensional regime.

arxiv-2403-06960.title: The MODEST catalog of depth-dependent spatially coupled inversions of sunspots observed by Hinode/SOT-SP
arxiv-2403-06960.creator: J. S. Castellanos Durán, N. Milanovic, A. Korpi-Lagg, B. Löptien, M. van Noort, S. K. Solanki
arxiv-2403-06960.description: Abstract We present a catalog that we named MODEST containing depth-dependent information on the atmospheric conditions inside sunspot groups of all types. The catalog is currently composed of 942 observations of 117 individual active regions with sunspots that cover all types of features observed in the solar photosphere.

arxiv-2405-15294.title: Semi-Supervised Learning guided by the Generalized Bayes Rule under Soft Revision
arxiv-2405-15294.creator: Stefan Dietrich, Julian Rodemann and Christoph Jansen
arxiv-2405-15294.description: Abstract We provide a theoretical and computational investigation of the Gamma-Maximin method with soft revision, which was recently proposed as a robust criterion for pseudo-label selection (PLS) in semi-supervised learning. Opposed to traditional methods for PLS we use credal sets of priors (“generalized Bayes”) to represent the epistemic modeling uncertainty.

arxiv-2412-06386.title: Estimation of Classical Cepheid’s Physical Parameters from NIR Light Curves
arxiv-2412-06386.creator: Lajos G. Balázs, Gábor B. Kovács
arxiv-2412-06386.description: Abstract Recent space-borne and ground-based observations provide photometric measurements as time series. The data points are nearly continuous over a limited observational interval or randomly scattered over a long period. The effect of interstellar dust extinction in the near-infrared range is only 10% of that measured in the visual (V) range.

pmc-10571557.title: Zebrafish in Lung Cancer Research
pmc-10571557.creator: Xiaodi Wu, Xin Hua, Ke Xu, Yong Song, Tangfeng Lv
pmc-10571557.description: Simple SummaryZebrafish is a crucial in vivo model for lung cancer research and is widely employed in studies focusing on cancer proliferation, metastasis, and angiogenesis. It plays a pivotal role in cancer drug development, being used for target validation, compound screening, and personalized therapy.

pmc-10650522.title: Real-Time 3D Object Detection on Crowded Pedestrians
pmc-10650522.creator: Bin Lu, Qing Li, Yanju Liang
pmc-10650522.description: In the field of autonomous driving, object detection under point clouds is indispensable for environmental perception. In order to achieve the goal of reducing blind spots in perception, many autonomous driving schemes have added low-cost blind-filling LiDAR on the side of the vehicle.

pmc-11619142.title: Ocular findings in Baraitser–Winter syndrome with a de novo mutation in the ACTG1 gene: a case report
pmc-11619142.creator: Jae Won Kim, Sook-Young Kim, Donghun Lee
pmc-11619142.description: BackgroundBaraitser–Winter syndrome (BWS) is rare, and no previous reports have described the visual course of patients with this condition. Herein, we report the long-term visual outcomes and ocular features of a 6-year-old patient diagnosed with BWS.Case presentationA 6-year-old female patient visited our clinic complaining of low vision.

pmc-12732174.title: High Household Transmission Among Asymptomatic Contacts Across Pandemic Waves in Cincinnati, Ohio
pmc-12732174.creator: Katherine Bowers, Stefanie Benoit, James Rose, Andrew F. Beck, Alonzo T. Folger, Tara N. Calhoun, Melissa E. Day, Andrew Lovell, Maryse Amin
pmc-12732174.description: Background/Objectives: COVID-19 and long COVID remain prevalent, with household transmission being an important mode of spread. To quantify household transmission of subclinical SARS-COV-2 infection and identify sociodemographic risk factors that may explain disparities in transmission, we conducted a case-ascertained antibody surveillance study of households in Cincinnati, Ohio.

pmc-13065620.title: Lewis Y (Ley) orchestrates leukocyte trafficking and inflammatory remodeling in leprosy patients from the Brazilian Amazon
pmc-13065620.creator: Sintia Almeida, Ermelinda do Rosário Moutinho da Cruz, Rosane do Socorro Pompeu de Loiola, Tereza C. O. Corvelo
pmc-13065620.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Leprosy is characterized by a complex inflammatory microenvironment in which host-related factors play a decisive role in disease progression. However, the contribution of tissue glycans to inflammatory remodeling remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the expression of Lewis blood group antigens in skin biopsies from patients with different clinical forms of leprosy in the Brazilian Amazon, a region marked by persistent hyperendemic transmission.

pmc-13081288.title: Political economy of adolescent mental health and well-being globally
pmc-13081288.creator: Olivia Biermann, Yusra Ribhi Shawar, Jeremy Shiffman, Seika L Brown, Miranda Bain, Ismahan Shire, Sarah Baird, Pamela Y Collins, Jennifer H Requejo, Augustina Mensa-Kwao, Mark Tomlinson, Asha George, Manasi Kumar, Zeus Aranda, Rita Tamambang, Olayinka Omigbodun, Stefan Swartling Peterson, Mariam Cla
pmc-13081288.description: BackgroundThe current generation of 1.3 billion adolescents (10–19-year-olds), most of whom live in low- and middle-income countries, face large and growing mental health problems. Collective action that could lead to significant improvement in adolescent mental health and well-being (AMH) remains limited.

pmc-13176942.title: Changes in the Activities of Daily Living and Associated Factors of Older Adults After Home‐Based Rehabilitation: A Multicenter Prospective 6‐Month Follow‐Up Study
pmc-13176942.creator: Shogo Kawada, Takami Maeno, Shoji Yokoya, Tetsuhiro Maeno
pmc-13176942.description: BackgroundOlder adults may experience changes in activities of daily living (ADL) after completing home‐based rehabilitation; however, no evidence exists regarding post‐rehabilitation outcomes and the factors influencing long‐term changes in ADL. This study aimed to investigate changes in ADL in older adults following home‐based rehabilitation and identify factors associated with these changes.

pmc-13435863.title: Suicide, quality of life, and psychotropic medication use in women with breast cancer
pmc-13435863.creator: Leonardo Felipe Ferreira de Carvalho, Adriana Inocenti Miasso, Leonardo Felipe Ferreira de Carvalho, Adriana Inocenti Miasso
pmc-13435863.description: Objectives:to identify factors associated with suicide risk, quality of life, and psychotropic medication use among women with breast cancer treated at an oncology hospital.Methods:a cross-sectional, descriptive, correlational study with a quantitative approach was conducted in the mastology outpatient clinic of a specialized oncology hospital. A total of 102 women participated and completed specific questionnaires.

pmc-13493823.title: Predicting gene essentiality and drug response from preclinical perturbation screens with layered ensemble of autoencoders and predictors
pmc-13493823.creator: Barbara Bodinier, Gaetan Dissez, Lucile Ter-Minassian, Linus Bleistein, Roberta Codato, John Klein, Eric Durand, Antonin Dauvin
pmc-13493823.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). High-throughput preclinical perturbation screens, where the effects of genetic, chemical, or environmental perturbations are systematically tested on disease models, hold significant promise for machine learning-enhanced drug discovery due to their scale and causal nature. Predictive models trained on such datasets can be used to (i) infer perturbation response for previously untested disease models, and (ii) characterise the biological context that affects perturbation response. Existing predictive models suffer from limited reproducibility, generalisability and interpretability.

pmc-13579525.title: Thermal and UV-light dual-mode hydroboration of nitriles catalyzed by Mo(CO)6
pmc-13579525.creator: Shu-Fen Hou, Shijie Dong, Yujian Zhao, Haiyan Niu, Ailing Zhang, Mengyuan Zhang, Zaiyong Jiang, Kaoxue Li, Chunling Xin, Xiqi Ma
pmc-13579525.description: Molybdenum, an early-transition metal, exhibits both biological activity and catalytic properties. It displays unique advantages in the activation of organic molecules, particularly nitrogen-containing substrates. Herein, the simple organometallic carbonyl complex Mo(CO)6 was employed as a pre-catalyst for the hydroboration of nitriles. Under thermal and photocatalytic conditions, aliphatic, aromatic, and cyclic nitriles were transformed into diborylated amines with excellent chemoselectivity.
